stages.title: Two lines at the top of the report code

screens.title: Add two lines at the top of the report code

open.what: One line lets the report use files. One line makes an empty table called dt that the whole report fills.
open.does: When it works, both new lines sit at the top of frmReport's code.

screens.title: Meet the six new words
screens.done: you have read the six words
screens.goal: I know the six new words before I type any of them.

blocks.p: Six new words come up in this chapter.

words: A table kept in memory, with columns and rows.
A list of words, one after another.
Code that runs again and again, once for each thing in a list.
Cuts one line into pieces at each ~.
The table you can see on the form.
Hides the rows that do not match. Empty words show every row.

stages.title: The Load event in four parts
stages.thing: the code as the report opens

screens.title: Type the code that runs as the report opens
screens.goal: This part types frmReport_Load in four chunks: columns, read the file, fill the rows, show the table.

open.what: frmReport_Load has four chunks. It makes the columns, reads the file, fills the rows and shows the table.
open.does: When it works, every saved pupil has a row in the table as the report opens.

screens.title: Give the table seven columns
screens.done: lines 3 to 9 are typed and the code has no red squiggles
screens.goal: When the report opens, the table gets seven columns, one for each thing it shows.

blocks.p: In the Design tab, double-click the title bar of frmReport.
frmReport_Load appears in the code tab.

code.title: The Load event of frmReport: code 1 of 4
code.where: between the curly brackets of frmReport_Load
partLines: Visual Studio wrote these two lines
Leave them as they are. Your code goes between the curly brackets.
given
The first four columns
Surname, Forename, Year and Gender. typeof string means each column holds words.
The last three columns
Quiz Score, Reaction Score and Group.
code.yours: MY report shows seven columns. Name the columns for what YOUR report must show.

screens.title: Read every line of the file
screens.done: lines 10 to 16 are typed, with one red squiggle that screen 4-4 clears
screens.goal: If the file is there, every line is read, and each line is cut into pieces at each ~.

blocks.p: File.Exists checks the file is there, then the [[for loop|2]] runs once for each line.
Each [[string[]|1]] is a list of words, and [[Split('~')|3]] cuts a line into pieces.

code.title: The Load event of frmReport: code 2 of 4
partLines: Is the file there?
An empty line. Then the rest only runs if the file is there.
Read every line
lines holds every line of the file.
Cut each line
For each line, parts holds its pieces, cut at each ~.
code.yours: MY file is pupilStats.txt. Type the same name YOU used in chapter 11, in both places.

blocks.watch: A red squiggle stays until screen 4-4 types the closing curly brackets. That is expected.

screens.title: See one line cut into eleven pieces
screens.done: you have looked at the picture and read the line under it
screens.goal: I see one saved line cut at every ~ into pieces numbered from 0.

blocks.p: This picture shows one saved line cut into its eleven pieces.

drawn.label: parts
drawn.alt: One saved line cut at every ~ into eleven pieces, numbered parts[0] to parts[10].
drawn.say: Count from 0. parts[0] is the first piece.

screens.title: Put the pieces in a row
screens.done: lines 17 to 27 are typed and the code has no red squiggles
screens.goal: Seven of the eleven pieces go into a new row of the table, in the order of the columns.

blocks.p: Each row takes the pieces in the same order as the columns.
The note on each line says which column.

code.title: The Load event of frmReport: code 3 of 4
partLines: A new row
dt.Rows.Add starts a new row of the table.
Seven pieces
Each line picks one piece by its number. The note says its column.
Close it all
The round bracket ends the row. Then the loop and the if end.

blocks.watch: Look at the numbers, not the order. The year is parts[3], but it is the third column.

blocks.yours: Use YOUR save line from chapter 11. Count its pieces from 0 to find the number of each one.
